title: Modesty, Shame is From Īmān
arabic_text: عَنْ [أَبِي مَسْعُودٍ عُقبةَ بنِ عَمْرٍو الأنصاريِّ الْبَدْريِّ] رَضِي اللهُ عَنْهُ قالَ: (قالَ messenger of Allah صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: "إِنَّ مِمَّا أَدْرَكَ النَّاسُ مِنْ كَلاَمِ النُّبُوَّةِ الأُولَى إِذَا لَمْ تَسْتَحِ فَاصْنَعْ مَا شِئْتَ").
english_translation: From Abū Masʿūd ʿUqbah bin ʾAmr al-Ansārī al-Badarī (raḍiyallāhu ʿanhu) who said: The Messenger of Allāh (ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wasallam) said, 'That which the people came across from the speech of the (era) of the first prophethood is that when you have no shame then do as you wish.'
description: This Hadith highlights the importance of shame and modesty as a deterrent from wrongdoing, implying that a lack of shame can lead one to do anything without moral restraint.
